why: Two backlog rows, nothing else. The only changed path is docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, appended through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row so the file's exact serialisation round-trips and no pre-existing line is re-attributed. No src/, no config/, no scripts/, no .github/workflows/, no order path, nothing enacted. Both findings were MEASURED while landing the MI-278 units and neither is fixed here, because both remedies are workflow or guard changes outside this lane's additive diff. (1) A PR that claude-pr-automerge OPENS never runs its pull_request checks: measured on #12031 over THREE separate real pushes, each producing exactly two check runs (watch, open-and-automerge -- the two that trigger on push) and zero of guards, pytest-collect, pytest-run, repo-inventory; positive control #12037 and #12019, same session and same push mechanism within the hour, got all six and #12019 merged, so it is not the runner, not an Actions outage and not the push method. The discriminator is that #12031 was opened by github-actions[bot]. CLAUDE.md's documented remedy for that trap -- 'push one ordinary commit' -- was followed three times and recovers the VISIBILITY of a check run but not the REQUIRED ones, so such a PR is permanently unmergeable by the ordinary route; the advice a few lines later in the same section, open the PR yourself FIRST and push the arming file second, is the one that holds. The obvious workaround is barred: the PR-activity rules forbid a close-and-reopen to kick CI, and that it would probably work here does not make it sanctioned. (2) Resolving a shared-register conflict by replaying 'my branch differs from its merge-base, so write mine' onto a MOVED main silently REVERTS rows another branch resolved -- it nearly reverted the three rows #12019 had landed minutes earlier, back to open. Every automated check would have passed: valid JSON in the right serialisation, correct row count, no id lost, and a status going backwards is not a shape error. It was caught only because the replay printed what it changed and the diff was read, i.e. by a habit rather than a mechanism. The correct rule, now used on all five of this session's PRs, is to replay only where main STILL HOLDS the merge-base value and to SKIP AND SAY SO where main has moved. This is deliberately NOT folded into the two merge-driver rows it resembles: those are a TOOL losing data during a merge, this is a replay reverting a DECISION after a merge that the tool handled correctly, and no driver can catch it because the reverted value is a legitimate value of the field. VERIFICATION on COMMITTED state: run_guards.py --event pull_request --base main; check_backlog_refs.py --base origin/main OK after it caught a TRUNCATED id in my own new row (the fourth such catch this session -- I quoted the OPEN-ITEMS-splice row's id without its -AND-EVERY-PROOF-THE-REPO-HAS-PASSES-OVER-IT tail; the truncated form is deliberately not written out here, because the ref guard cannot tell a truncated id from an invented one and would flag this file for naming it); check_claim_basis.py --base origin/main.
